sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian verbs change according to the subject. In the indefinite present, common first-person forms often end in -ok/-ek/-ök.

English needs a separate pronoun to show who’s acting (‘I work’), but Hungarian packs that information straight into the verb ending — dolgoz- + -om already says ‘I work’ with no én required. This is exactly why you’ll soon see sentences with no pronoun at all and still know precisely who’s doing what.
